articles.title: ‘Australia has given me pathway, not a place in team’: Anaya Bangar on WBBL dream
articles.summary: Cricket News: Anaya Bangar's return to competitive cricket now has a potential timeline, with March 2027 set as the key date in her bid to pursue elite women's cric.
articles.body: Anaya Bangar's return to competitive cricket now has a potential timeline, with March 2027 set as the key date in her bid to pursue elite women's cricket in Australia and potentially earn a route into the Women's Big Bash League.The former Mumbai U-19 cricketer has been cleared by Cricket Australia to play community cricket and has been given a pathway to pursue elite women's cricket, subject to the governing body's eligibility requirements.Bangar, the daughter of former India cricketer and ex-India batting coach Sanjay Bangar, stressed that the clearance does not amount to selection for the WBBL or automatic entry into elite cricket. Instead, it gives her an opportunity to work towards that level.“I am preparing to return to women’s cricket in Australia with the aim of pursuing elite cricket from March 2027,” the 25-year-old said. “This has not been an automatic or an informal process. Cricket Australia has a framework designed to balance fairness, competitive integrity, and inclusion in women’s sport, and my case has been considered through that framework.”Bangar said she understands that she will have to earn any opportunity that comes her way.“Cricket Australia has given me a pathway, which does not mean that I have been given a place in a team. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,” she said.March 2027 eligibility checkpointBangar's immediate plan is to find a club and play community cricket in Australia as she works towards a return to the competitive game. Her participation in elite competitions, including the WBBL, will depend on Cricket Australia's Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy.Under the policy, a player's serum testosterone concentration must remain below 10 nmol/L for at least 12 months to qualify for elite cricket.Bangar's eligibility will be assessed from March 2027, including through a required blood test.“My understanding from Cricket Australia's clearance is that my eligibility for elite women's cricket from March 2027 remains subject to the applicable policy requirements, including a blood test assessment at the same time. If that March 2027 test confirms that I continue to meet the required testosterone criteria, I will be eligible to pursue selection for elite women’s cricket, including the Women’s Big Bash League pathway,” Bangar said.Meeting those requirements would allow Bangar to seek selection, but would not guarantee her a place in an elite team.“I don’t expect my history or my identity to earn me a place on a cricket team. I want my cricket to earn me a place on a cricket team,” she said.Why Bangar approached Cricket AustraliaBangar had earlier sought clarity from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) over whether transgender athletes could compete in women's cricket in India. She said she received no response to a letter submitted last year.She subsequently approached Cricket Australia in June this year.According to Bangar, Cricket Australia assessed her medical records, blood tests, documents relating to her surgeries and a research report from Manchester Metropolitan University's Institute of Sport before reaching its decision.“After I published my athlete testing report and everything else, BCCI stayed quiet about it. Whereas Cricket Australia actually read my report, went through all my medical history and had a proper team assessing my case,” Bangar said.“I approached Cricket Australia and they gave me clearance to play in terms of fairness and inclusivity.”Bangar is now looking for a club in Australia, with community cricket set to be the first step in her attempt to rebuild her playing career and eventually pursue an opportunity in elite women's cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Sonal Dinusha continued his impressive run against India by registering his fourth consecutive fifty-plus score in Test cricket on Thursday, putting his name alongside some of the game's most celebrated batters.The Sri Lankan left-hander reached the landmark during the final day of the second Test in Colombo, where his resilient innings helped the hosts keep their hopes of saving the match alive. Dinusha's latest half-century came after he had already produced three substantial scores across the two-Test series.𝟓𝟎-𝐩𝐥𝐮𝐬 𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐟𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚Douglas Jardine (ENG, 1932-1934)Everton Weekes (WI, 1948)Clyde Walcott (WI, 1948)Ken Barrington (ENG, 1959)Sonal Dinusha (SL, 2026)Dinusha began the series with a century and an 84 in the first Test. He joins Kumar Sangakkara and Dimuth Karunaratne in achieving the feat.Sangakkara accomplished it against Bangladesh at home in 2013 and against England in England in 2014, while Karunaratne achieved the feat against South Africa at home in 2018.Dinusha's achievement against India is even rarer. He is only the second batter to score fifty-plus in each of his first four Test innings against India.The only previous batter to achieve that feat was Zimbabwe great Andy Flower during Zimbabwe's tour of India in 2000. Flower's scores across the four innings were 183*, 70, 55 and 232*.Dinusha has also entered another exclusive list involving India. He is the fifth batter to score fifty-plus in each of his first four Test innings against the country.England's Douglas Jardine achieved the feat between 1932 and 1934, while West Indies legends Everton Weekes and Clyde Walcott did so in 1948. England's Ken Barrington followed in 1959.Dinusha's latest contribution came at a crucial stage for Sri Lanka. His half-century, combined with a century partnership with Keshara Nuwantha, allowed the hosts to negotiate the first session of the final day without losing a wicket and maintain their hopes of securing a draw.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sonal Dinusha becomes third Sri Lankan to achieve this feat against India
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sonal Dinusha stood tall for Sri Lanka and scored a defiant century to keep India at bay on Day 5 of the second Test in Colombo.Dinusha was unbeaten o.
articles.body: Sonal Dinusha stood tall for Sri Lanka and scored a defiant century to keep India at bay on Day 5 of the second Test in Colombo.Dinusha was unbeaten on 98 at tea and did not have to wait long to complete his century. On the first ball of the third and final session, he flicked Mohammed Siraj towards mid-wicket for a couple of runs to reach the landmark.It was another brilliant innings from the Sri Lankan batter, who continued his sublime run in the two-match Test series against India.Three centuries in the two-Test seriesDinusha had already scored a century in the first Test in Galle, where Sri Lanka suffered a 165-run defeat. He continued his fine form in the second Test, scoring 103 runs in the first innings. With Sri Lanka under pressure to save the Test and avoid a 2-0 series whitewash, Dinusha once again rose to the occasion and scored another hundred.His latest century gave him three hundreds in the two-match series. He became only the third Sri Lankan batter to score three centuries in a two-match Test series.He also joined an elite group of batters who have scored three hundreds in a two-Test series. Dinusha is now one of nine players to achieve the feat.Only the 12th batter to do it against IndiaOverall, Dinusha became the 12th batter to score centuries in both innings of a Test against India. More importantly, he is only the second batter to achieve the feat against India since January 2015. The previous batter to do so was England's Jonny Bairstow, who scored 106 and an unbeaten 114 against India at Edgbaston in 2022.Dinusha's 103 in the first innings and unbeaten 100 in the second innings have now put him in that elite group. Third Sri Lankan to achieve the feat against IndiaDinusha also became only the third Sri Lankan batter to score centuries in both innings of a Test against India. Duleep Mendis was the first Sri Lankan to do it, scoring 105 in both innings against India in Chennai in 1982. Aravinda de Silva was the second. He scored 146 and 120 at the Colombo SSC against India in 1997.Now, Dinusha has become the third Sri Lankan to join the list. His scores of 103 and 100 not out came at the Colombo SSC in 2026.Duleep Mendis - 105 & 105 - Chennai, 1982Aravinda de Silva - 146 & 120 - Colombo (SSC), 1997Sonal Dinusha - 103 & 100* - Colombo (SSC), 2026Most hundreds in a two-match Test seriesAravinda de Silva is the only player to feature twice on the list. He scored three centuries against Pakistan at home in 1997 and repeated the feat against India at home later that year. South Africa's Jacques Kallis scored three hundreds against Pakistan away from home in 2007, while Hashim Amla scored three against India away from home in 2010.Kumar Sangakkara scored three centuries for Sri Lanka against Bangladesh at home in 2013. Pakistan's Younis Khan then scored three hundreds against Australia at a neutral venue in 2014.Australia's Marnus Labuschagne scored three centuries against West Indies at home in 2022, while New Zealand's Kane Williamson did the same against South Africa at home in 2024.Dinusha is the latest name on the list after scoring three hundreds against India at home in 2026.3 - Aravinda de Silva (SL) vs PAK (Home, 1997)3 - Aravinda de Silva (SL) vs IND (Home, 1997)3 - Jacques Kallis (SA) vs PAK (Away, 2007)3 - Hashim Amla (SA) vs IND (Away, 2010)3 - Kumar Sangakkara (SL) vs BAN (Home, 2013)3 - Younis Khan (PAK) vs AUS (Neutral, 2014)3 - Marnus Labuschagne (AUS) vs WI (Home, 2022)3 - Kane Williamson (NZ) vs SA (Home, 2024)3 - Sonal Dinusha (SL) vs IND (Home, 2026)Eighth Sri Lankan to score hundreds in both inningsDinusha's 103 in the first innings and his unbeaten 100 in the second innings also helped him achieve another major feat. He became the eighth Sri Lankan batter to score centuries in both innings of a Test.Aravinda de Silva and Kumar Sangakkara are the only two players on the list to have achieved the feat twice. The other Sri Lankan batters to do it are Duleep Mendis, Asanka Gurusinha, Tillakaratne Dilshan, Dhananjaya de Silva and Kamindu Mendis.The list shows how rare Dinusha's achievement is. Several great Sri Lankan batters, including Sangakkara and Aravinda, have achieved it, while only eight Sri Lankan players have managed to score a century in both innings of a Test.Aravinda de Silva (twice)Kumar Sangakkara (twice)Duleep MendisAsanka GurusinhaTillakaratne DilshanDhananjaya de SilvaKamindu MendisSonal DinushaGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan-born ODI cricketer handed 15-month ban by ICC; here's why
articles.summary: Cricket News: UAE batter Asif Khan has been banned for 15 months after testing positive for a banned anabolic steroid during an out-of-competition doping test condu.
articles.body: UAE batter Asif Khan has been banned for 15 months after testing positive for a banned anabolic steroid during an out-of-competition doping test conducted last year.Asif tested positive for a metabolite of mesterolone in a sample collected on September 8, 2025. Mesterolone is an anabolic steroid used to increase testosterone levels.The 36-year-old admitted to violating Article 2.1 of the ICC Anti-Doping Code and accepted the sanction through a Case Resolution Agreement with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and the International Cricket Council (ICC)."The 36-year-old admitted to a violation of Article 2.1 of the ICC Anti-Doping Code and accepted the sanction through a Case Resolution Agreement with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and the International Cricket Council (ICC)," read a statement from cricket's world governing body.The ban has been backdated to September 8, 2025 and will run until December 7, 2026. Asif will be allowed to resume training with a team or use the facilities of a club or other ICC Member organisation from October 8, but he will only be eligible to return to competitive cricket from December 8."Asif will be permitted to return to training with a team or use the facilities of a club or other ICC Member organisation from October 8, but will only be eligible to return to competitive cricket from December 8," the ICC statement said.The ICC has also disqualified Asif's individual results from September 8, 2025 until the start of his provisional suspension on December 29, 2025."This includes all resulting consequences, such as the loss of any medals, points, prize money or prizes."Asif, who was born in Pakistan and moved to the UAE in 2017, has represented the UAE in 38 ODIs and 56 T20 Internationals since making his international debut in 2022.Before moving to the UAE, the right-handed batter played 32 first-class matches in Pakistan's domestic cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'People will lose interest in Pakistan cricket': Moin Khan slams PCB, selectors
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Moin Khan has warned that the country could find it increasingly difficult to arrange bilateral series with top tea.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Moin Khan has warned that the country could find it increasingly difficult to arrange bilateral series with top teams if the national side continues to struggle. Moin, who played 69 Tests and 219 ODIs for Pakistan, also criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and the national selectors for the way the cricket system has been handled in recent years.'People will lose interest in Pakistan cricket'Moin said Pakistan have struggled across formats, particularly in Test cricket. He fears the situation could get worse if the team's poor results continue."We have been struggling in all formats but notably in test matches and if this trend continues I am afraid people will lose interest in Pakistan cricket," Moin said on a podcast.He warned that Pakistan could slip down the cricketing order and face problems in attracting top teams for bilateral series."We might find ourselves relegated to the bottom half of the cricket world finding it difficult to get bilateral series with top teams."I blame the frequent changes being made by the board in the cricket system including appointments/removal of captains, coaches, players and the inexplicable calls made by the national selectors."Unless you don’t have continuity, stability and faith in a captain, coach or players, how can you expect to achieve good results," he said.Frequent changes hurting Pakistan cricketMoin said repeated changes in domestic cricket and the national team have affected Pakistan badly. According to him, the uncertainty has also resulted in players losing confidence in the system.The former wicketkeeper-batter also said the PCB often makes decisions based on the people in power at a particular time rather than following a consistent institutional approach."Whenever a chairman and management team is changed you see things change in our cricket system which are not necessarily productive. So where is the stability?," he asked.Moin questions players' prioritiesMoin also held some of the players responsible for the current situation. He expressed disappointment with the approach of players who, according to him, are not spending enough time improving their skills and cricketing temperament."I don’t want to harp on the past but to me it seems most players nowadays don’t give enough time to developing their skills and cricket temperament. It is more about how much money we can make in leagues rather than setting and reaching personal goals of excellence as a cricketer.”He said financial rewards would follow if a player first focused on performing successfully for the national team."When I played we earned in lakhs. Nowadays players earn in crores but players must also remember nothing is greater than playing for your country with success."'Priorities have changed'Moin said he had given similar advice to his son, Azam Khan, who has played T20 internationals for Pakistan. He said representing the country should take priority over private leagues."I guess priorities have changed for players now. The PCB and selectors have not helped by devaluing the Pakistan cap,” he added.According to Moin, playing for Pakistan in his time required considerable hard work, sacrifice and preparation.He recalled how preparation helped him perform under pressure."People ask me how you always got runs in a crisis situation and I tell them it is all about how well you prepare as a player for the matches."Concern over Pakistan's pace bowlingMoin also expressed concern about the current state of pace bowling in Pakistan. He said bowlers need to put in more hours to develop their skills and improve their pace."Bowlers are not willing to put in the hours. I played with greats like Wasim Akram, Waqar Younis, Shoaib Akhtar and I can tell you the perfection of bowling on any sort of pitch and increased pace only comes when you put in long hours in the nets.”Moin said the great fast bowlers he played alongside worked extremely hard on their skills and fitness. He made it clear all these greats worked very hard on their skills and fitness by themselves.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Colombo draw tastes like defeat as Sri Lanka dent India's WTC final hopes
articles.summary: Cricket News: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: With the handshake looming, Shubman Gill introduced himself into the attack. Judging by their body language, India had al.
articles.body: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: With the handshake looming, Shubman Gill introduced himself into the attack. Judging by their body language, India had already checked out of the fixture with Sri Lanka's lead over 200 runs and little time remaining. A result in India's favour was almost out of the equation and the visitors were waiting for the formalities to be completed. Yashasvi Jaiswal was introduced from the other end, and even Dhruv Jurel rolled his arm over as the writing was on the cards. India would rue drawing a Test they were in a very good position of winning, squandering the opportunity to bolster their World Test Championship (WTC) final chances.Sometimes, draws feel like wins and Sri Lanka must have a similar feeling in Colombo. With chips down and backs to the wall, Sonal Dinusha produced a performance for the ages, who had an equally stubborn lower-order for company. He has been the rockstar for the hosts in this series and made India dance to his tunes when he battled for close to two days to eke out a hard-fought draw. The 25-year-old's sequence of scores in the series read 100, 84, 103 and 133*, and across the four innings his compact technique, composure and solid temperament stood out.It wasn't easy; whenever he came out to bat, the team was in a spot of bother and he mostly had the lower-order and tail for company. In the second Test alone, he spent nearly 147 overs out in the middle, facing 71 overs, frustrating the visitors and keeping the win out of their reach.It didn't help that Mohammed Siraj wasn't running in with the steam he would have liked and the pitch offered turn but not enough threat. The tone was set by the pair of Keshara Nuwantha and Dinusha for over 40 overs and the former ended up playing 150 deliveries in the process. Lahiru Kumara and Asitha Fernando followed the drill and India just carried on in hopes of things miraculously falling into place.The 116th over of the Sri Lankan innings was significant in more ways than one. Siraj patiently waited to bowl as Sarfaraz Khan suggested field changes to Shubman Gill before the fast bowler began. The short-ball trap was set. After trying it for two deliveries, which Sonal Dinusha ducked safely, the bowler walked up to the stumps and flipped the bails. This was India's second attempt, followed by a very creative field setting, likely the first of its kind that day.The entire field moved towards the off-side, placing enough men in catching positions for a miscued drive. Dinusha had been pushed back for most of the over and here Siraj was trying to induce a false shot from the most consistent batter of the series. The plan didn't work but India's attempt to finally make things happen brought success when Prabath Jayasuriya was dismissed in the very next over while driving against Ravindra Jadeja. India, even after picking up two wickets in the first hour after Lunch, were still two wickets away from beginning their chase but that 12-ball period summed up a story of what could have, and should have, been for India in the first session.The pitch was flat, the body language was flatter and the tactics the flattest. The open fields and the focus solely on dismissing Dinusha's partner not only allowed desperation to creep in but also prevented sustained pressure, as there were easy runs available, meaning the left-hander didn't need to take risks. India were again guilty of going through the motions and the defensive ploys were baffling to say the least at a time when wickets were needed.India, however, focused on cutting off boundaries, allowing easy singles and even keeping fielders positioned for a reverse-sweep. In a Test match! It was a period where shoulders started dropping, leaving India head coach Gautam Gambhir with no option but to summon captain Gill to the change room before the lunch break.The skipper spoke to coach Gambhir and video analyst Hari Prasad Mohan when nothing was going their way in the first session. They took the new ball, tried different combinations, played around with the field, albeit defensively, but none worked. Despite being in a position of absolute control, India played catch-up. However, with the weather gods permitting and the advantage of the first-innings run cushion, they always had the best chance of securing a favourable result.Across the two innings, Sri Lanka's lower-order, apart from the usual suspect Dinusha, remained the thorn in the flesh as they collectively faced 71 overs deliveries. This will require a lot of introspection and the team needs to be tactically better for tougher shores in future. It took India 44.1 overs to wrap up the tail in the first innings, but they couldn't do that in more than 90 overs in the second. The runs were never the question but the hosts were wiping off crucial time from the fixture, hoping the dark clouds would rescue them and help force the best result: a draw.The hosts fought for a draw - a result which looked extremely unlikely. The weather allowed India a proper crack at the opposition but the resistance from Sri Lanka's lower-order not only avoided the whitewash but also dealt a major dent to India's WTC final qualification hopes. With just one win, they now have no room to slip in the remaining seven Tests - two away against New Zealand and five at home against Australia.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: For the first time against India and only the fourth time overall, Sri Lanka did the unthinkable in Colombo. After being forced to follow on and facing a huge 213-run first-innings deficit, Sri Lanka fought back brilliantly to save the second Test against India on Thursday. The match ended in a draw, with India winning the two-match series 1-0.Sri Lanka break a long follow-on jinxSri Lanka had lost 24 of their previous 27 Tests after being asked to follow on. Even more strikingly, they had lost all eight such Tests against India.But in Colombo, the hosts finally broke that run.Resuming at 229/6 on the final day, Sri Lanka finished on 429/9 before the teams agreed to call off the match. Sonal Dinusha led the resistance with an unbeaten 133, while Keshara Nuwantha scored 46. The pair added 112 runs for the seventh wicket.This was only the fourth time Sri Lanka had managed to save a Test after being asked to follow on.Sri Lanka saving Tests after follow-onvs Zimbabwe, Bulawayo, 1994 — 193/4vs England, Lord's, 2006 — 537/9vs West Indies, Galle, 2010 — 241/4vs India, Colombo SSC, 2026 — 429/9Dinusha completes a remarkable seriesDinusha was at the heart of Sri Lanka's resistance. He had scored 103 in the first innings of the Colombo Test and hit his maiden Test century in the series opener in Galle. His unbeaten 133 took his tally to three centuries in the two-Test series.He also became only the third batter to score centuries in both innings of a Test while following on.Hundreds in both innings, second while following onVijay Hazare — 116 & 145 vs Australia, Adelaide, 1948Andy Flower — 142 & 199* vs South Africa, Harare, 2001Sonal Dinusha — 103 & 133* vs India, Colombo SSC, 2026For India, Manav Suthar finished with 3/121 and Ravindra Jadeja took 3/94. articles.title: 'Draw not hurting like a defeat': Shubman Gill after Sri Lanka deny India 2-0 clean sweep
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India had looked set to complete a 2-0 series sweep against Sri Lanka, but the hosts produced a stubborn fightback to force a draw in the s.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India had looked set to complete a 2-0 series sweep against Sri Lanka, but the hosts produced a stubborn fightback to force a draw in the second Test in Colombo.Sri Lanka were bowled out for 290 in their first innings after India declared on 503/9. India captain Shubman Gill then enforced the follow-on, hoping his bowlers could finish the job and seal another big win.But Sonal Dinusha had other plans.The Sri Lankan batter scored his third century of the two-match series and remained unbeaten on 133 as Sri Lanka reached 429/9 before the players shook hands for a draw.'Draw not hurting like a defeat'Despite missing out on a 2-0 series win, Gill said the result was not as painful as a defeat. He also praised Sri Lanka for their effort while admitting India were disappointed after aiming for another victory."Draw not hurting like a defeat… situation wise, draw was credit to them, we hoped for a win so disappointing"Gill also said the Test provided valuable lessons for him as captain."Things always don’t go as per plan, so lot of learnings for me as well as a captain. I give 10/10 for the effort and intent of everyone."India eventually finished the series with a 1-0 win after their 165-run victory in the first Test in Galle.Gill defends follow-on decisionGill also explained why he chose to enforce the follow-on after India gained a big lead. With rain a possibility, he wanted to give India enough time to push for victory.India had taken a 213-run first-innings lead and had Sri Lanka under pressure after enforcing the follow-on. However, Dinusha once again stood between India and victory.Resuming at 229/6, Dinusha and Keshara Nuwantha put together a crucial 112-run partnership for the seventh wicket. Nuwantha made 46, while Dinusha carried his bat through the innings.India tried different approaches on a fifth-day pitch, but the conditions became increasingly difficult for the bowlers.Manav Suthar finished with 3/121 from 41 overs, while Ravindra Jadeja took 3/94 in 38.3 overs."I don’t think follow-on backfired, we fielded for over 250 overs. We were anticipating (rain), wanted to take that chance. Had we not taken and had it rained, you would have asked why no follow on."'Sri Lanka played really well'Gill admitted that Sri Lanka deserved credit for their resistance, especially over the final three days."Sri Lanka played really well. articles.title: Shubman Gill dismisses Mohammed Siraj's injury concerns, says it 'takes time to come back to rhythm'
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India captain Shubman Gill on Thursday ruled out any injury concern for Mohammed Siraj after the pacer appeared to be below his best during.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India captain Shubman Gill on Thursday ruled out any injury concern for Mohammed Siraj after the pacer appeared to be below his best during the drawn second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo.Siraj bowled at a reduced pace and often used a shorter run-up during the Test. His fitness also came under the scanner after he landed heavily while trying to take a catch in Sri Lanka's first innings.Gill, however, made it clear that Siraj was not carrying an injury.'Firstly, Siraj is not injured'Gill said Siraj had not been feeling his best even during the first Test in Galle and was also returning to international cricket after a break.“Firstly, Siraj is not injured. He didn't feel well even in the first match (at Galle). He last played against Afghanistan in June…so he was playing almost after a couple of months. It takes time for someone to come back to the rhythm.“Even in the first Test, we felt that his pace was slow. But sometimes when you play more, you come back to the rhythm. But as far as the injury is concerned, there is nothing,” he said.Siraj's lack of his usual pace was noticeable as India struggled to finish off Sri Lanka on the fifth day. The hosts batted through the final day, with Sonal Dinusha scoring an unbeaten 133 to secure a draw.'It gets very frustrating'India had reduced Sri Lanka to 229/6 by the end of the fourth day but could not force the remaining wickets on the final day.“It gets very frustrating. We attacked a lot in the beginning. But I think as the match went on, the wicket got slower. It was not like the ball was not moving and when the ball was spinning, the wickets were not in play. It was not like the wicket was very flat,” said Gill at the post-match press meet.The India captain said Sri Lanka's defensive approach made it difficult for his bowlers to create chances.“Unless you are playing a shot and looking to make a run, then it is difficult to take a wicket. We tried all that we could, and I don't think there was any lack of intensity or the efforts that we put in. The spinners bowled 50-60 overs on the trot for three days.“Fielding for three days is not an easy task in these conditions. I would say 10 out of 10 for the effort and the intent. They also played really well,” he added.Gill also felt India could have been in a better position if they had taken their chances on the fourth day.“On day 4, we thought we had created chances. If there was a little more pressure, the wickets would have come and then maybe the result would have been better. But as long as we still have a chance to qualify for the World Test Championship (final), it’s fine.”Gill praises PrasidhGill was pleased with the progress made by Prasidh Krishna.“I think he's been in the pick of our bowlers. When things are not happening, he's been our go-to bowler, especially this season. He's created chances, which is what I want as a captain. We want a go-to bowler when wickets are not guaranteed. articles.title: 'It gets very frustrating': Shubman Gill coming to terms with the captaincy challenge
articles.summary: Cricket News: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: In his first press conference of the tour, Shubman Gill termed qualifying for the World Test Championship as the \"ultimat.
articles.body: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: In his first press conference of the tour, Shubman Gill termed qualifying for the World Test Championship as the "ultimate goal," a sentiment he maintained while preparing to leave the country. In between his two media interactions, the Indian captain saw his team register a comprehensive win in Galle and then settle for a draw in a fixture they were well positioned to win in Colombo. Although the series was won, the trophy secured, and his undefeated run as captain checked off crucial boxes, India left behind crucial WTC points needed to boost their win percentage.As captain, he had his most challenging few days under the sun in Colombo when Sonal Dinusha and the Sri Lanka's tail frustrated the visitors and prevented them from getting the result they desperately wanted. There were moments he would helplessly stand and observe from the short-cover position, have an intense chat with head coach Gautam Gambhir when nothing worked and then even egg his teammates on when their shoulders started dropping."It gets very frustrating," he said regarding the challenges, explaining the questions that follow. "Was follow-on the best decision, was it not? But then you have to go back in the moment and see, what can I do? Did I make the best decision in that moment? Yes, I did. Then you can't do anything about it. You have to keep trying your best, and I think we did that," added the Indian captain.While they struggled to remove the Sri Lankan tail in both innings, Gill was not ready to pin the blame on any of his teammates and lauded their effort."We tried all that we could, and at the end of the day, even from the players, you can expect them giving their 100%, their top efforts, and I don't think there was any lacking in intensity or the efforts that we put in," said Gill.Highlighting the volume of overs the spinners bowled on a surface which became easier to bat as the game progressed, Gill gave them 10/10 for effort and intent, and continued to focus on the ultimate goal - the World Test Championship."The spinners bowled 50-60 overs on the trot for three days. Fielding for three days is not an easy task in these conditions with the heat. In terms of effort, I would say 10 out of 10 for the effort and the intent. A lot of learning, so many things won't always go as you plan, but as long as we still have a chance to qualify for the World Test Championship," added Gill.India operated with in-out field positions for most of the match, offering significant protection against the sweep, especially when Sonal Dinusha was at the crease. While it did open up easy singles, Gill felt there couldn't have been a better plan as the slow turn off the surface meant bowled and LBW were the dismissals out of the equation."The ball was spinning but the wickets were not in play. As a batsman, if you know that your bowlers do not have 2 modes of dismissal in play, then it becomes easier to bat. Unless you are playing shot and not looking to make a run, then it is difficult to take a wicket," said Gill."They were sweeping, step out and you also have to have your close-in fielders for the catch. So there was a lot of in-and-out field and there was always a lefty and a righty batting. So it's especially on a wicket like this it's difficult to have a field on one side," added Gill on his field placements.With the series won and positives accumulated, Gill asserted that they still have a good chance to qualify for the WTC final. The Indian captain is hopeful to do well in New Zealand and be in a better position by the time Australia come for the Border Gavaskar Trophy early next year."I still think we've got a pretty good chance to qualify for the WTC. If we play the New Zealand series well and then hopefully, by the time the Australia series comes, we just have to win the series. If we're in a situation where we just have to win the series, I think we'll be in a good position to qualify for the WTC. A lot of solidity and a lot of confidence in our betting lineup, for sure. I always feel if you put up runs in test matches, three and a half, four sessions, you're always in the game."We've got bowlers that can make up 20 wickets. As long as we keep putting 350-400 runs consistently on the board, we'll always be in the game and looking at our batting performances, it's very pleasing to see that we are doing that," said Gill.There is still time before India start preparing for their next Test assignment. For now, the immediate focus will be on recovering after the grind in Galle and Colombo, and then hoping the best pool of players are available when the selectors assemble to pick squads for the New Zealand tour.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India's draw against Sri Lanka in the second Test at the Colombo SSC has made their road to the World Test Championship final tougher.Sri Lanka held India to a draw after a remarkable fightback on the fifth day. As a result, India won the two-Test series 1-0 instead of completing a 2-0 sweep.The draw gave India 16 points from the Sri Lanka series instead of the maximum 24. India now sit fifth in the WTC points table with a PCT of 51.52.With Bangladesh drawing their series in Australia 1-1, the race for the two WTC final spots has become more interesting as the competition moves into its next phase.What India need to doIndia have seven Tests left in the current WTC cycle. They will first play two Tests away from home against New Zealand before hosting Australia for a five-Test series.Series left for IndiaNew Zealand: 2 Tests (away)Australia: 5 Tests (home)The simplest path for India is to win all seven matches. If they do that, they will finish with a PCT of 70.37, which should put them in a very strong position to reach the final.WTC points table after India-Sri Lanka TestTeamMatchesWonLostDrawPointsPCTAustralia108209680.00South Africa43103675.00New Zealand64115272.22Bangladesh63214055.56India115426851.52Sri Lanka61232433.33England145815029.76West Indies122823020.83Pakistan72501619.05Six wins could take India close to 65 PCTIndia can also afford one defeat in their remaining seven Tests. articles.title: From washing utensils in Kolkata to a career-best 167: Shahbaz Ahmed's remarkable cricket journey
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: True ambition rarely follows a straight path. For Shahbaz Ahmed, pursuing a career in elite-level cricket meant walking away from an establ.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: True ambition rarely follows a straight path. For Shahbaz Ahmed, pursuing a career in elite-level cricket meant walking away from an established life, making extreme personal sacrifices, and rebuilding his dreams from scratch over 1,500 kilometers away from home.Born in Mewat, Haryana, Shahbaz was on a traditional career track, pursuing a degree in civil engineering. His father wanted him to secure a stable corporate future, but Shahbaz had a different vision. Deep down, he knew his heart belonged to the 22 yards of a cricket pitch, not blueprint designs.Taking an enormous leap of faith, he decided to leave his engineering studies on hold and packed his bags for Kolkata. Moving roughly 1,500 kilometers away from his hometown to the heartland of West Bengal, Shahbaz was determined to make it in the ultra-competitive Kolkata club circuit.Hardship, Hustle, and grinding on the MaidansArriving in Kolkata without guaranteed contacts or financial security, the young all-rounder experienced the harsh reality of living on a shoestring budget. During his early days chasing opportunities across the famous Kolkata Maidans, Shahbaz endured severe financial strain.To stay afloat and cover basic living expenses, he washed utensils and took up odd tasks while living in local club quarters and modest accommodation.Even while fighting for survival, his commitment to cricket never wavered.He carried engineering textbooks alongside his cricket kit to keep his family's condition afloat while spending every remaining hour of daylight training under the sun.Breaking into the spotlightHis break came when local club Tapan Memorial gave him a chance in Division 1 club cricket. Shahbaz grabbed it with both hands, scorching the local scene by scoring six hundreds in seven matches alongside a heap of wickets.His cerebral understanding of angles, a trait he credited to his love for geometry, turned him into an invaluable asset.His domestic consistency soon earned him a debut for Bengal in the Ranji Trophy, followed by a coveted IPL contract. Known for his crisp left-handed middle-order hitting and pin-point left-arm orthodox spin, Shahbaz quickly became Bengal's crisis man.His impressive outings paved the way for an international call-up, making his ODI debut for Team India against South Africa in October 2022 and later playing in the 2023 Asian Games.Reviving India hopesAfter drifting out of national reckoning, Shahbaz made a statement in the opening leg of the domestic season. Representing East Zone in the Duleep Trophy against North East Zone, he showcased his full repertoire as a elite match-winner.Slotted in the lower middle-order, Shahbaz shepherded the tail to orchestrate a massive total of 467. He was the last man out, scoring a career-best 167 in first-class cricket—an innings packed with 17 boundaries and four sixes across 80 overs.Returning to the field with the ball, his left-arm spin ripped through the opposition batting order, picking up 3 for 20 in 10 overs to enforce a follow-on and wrap up a massive victory inside three days.From washing dishes and skipping semester exams to firing off career-best performances on the big stage, Shahbaz Ahmed’s journey serves as a powerful reminder that pure determination can break down any barrier.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Jamie Smith and Jordan Cox battle in second Test at Lord's
articles.summary: Jamie Smith and Jordan Cox battle difficult conditions and an improved Pakistan performance to take England to a competitive total on the opening day of the second Test.
articles.body:
Second Rothesay Test, Lord's (day one of five)

England 248-9: Smith 61, Cox 55; Abbas 4-56

Jamie Smith and Jordan Cox battled difficult conditions and an improved Pakistan performance to take England to a competitive total on the opening day of the second Test.

In the damp and gloom at Lord's, Smith made 61 and Cox 55 to take England to 248-9 on a first day that was delayed by rain and curtailed by bad light.

The value of the hosts' score will only be revealed in time. The Lord's pitch is much better than the poor surface used for England's win against New Zealand in June, while more rain is forecast for the next three days.

It could be that England have batted themselves into a position from where they can win this match and the series, which would be a successful end to a troubling week dominated by the Brydon Carse controversy.

Cox was again impressive in only his third Test. He added 67 for the for sixth wicket with Smith, who looked fluent for a much-needed half-century.

England were boosted by a late cameo of 34 not out from Gus Atkinson, while Pakistan were led by four wickets from Muhammad Abbas and three from Mohammad Ali. Things could have better for the tourists had they not dropped three catches.

Under a dark sky and with the floodlights on, England would probably have wanted to bowl before the day was out, only for the light to end proceedings.

England close on 248-9 against Pakistan - day one as it happened

Durham will pick bowler Carse until told otherwise

TMS podcast: Abbas masterclass as Smith stars on day one

England battle on the field after tough week off it

For England, the chance to win their first Test series since 2024 comes after yet another off-field drinking incident.

Carse was removed from the squad for this Test after a night out in Derby on Saturday, with police investigating allegations of an assault. Carse is in the Durham side for their ongoing County Championship match against Gloucestershire.

The home side steamrollered Pakistan at Headingley in Joe Root's first Test back as captain. It was always likely Pakistan would improve on their performance from Leeds, simply because the tourists could not play much worse.

Pakistan were boosted by the return of captain Babar Azam from a hand injury, in the side for Salman Ali Agha who skippered in Leeds. Babar's first impact was to call correctly and play finally got under way at 12:20 BST.

The tourists' trio of fast-medium seamers were ideally suited to the conditions and they showed much greater control than last week.

England were sometimes wasteful - Dan Lawrence ran himself out and Harry Brook was bowled driving - and sometimes unlucky - Emilio Gay was caught down the leg side. For the most part, the batters were happy to roll up their sleeves, another encouraging sign early in Root's second reign.

The result was a compelling contest, an arm wrestle with neither side ever able to claim they held the upper hand.

England's total seems at least workable, yet Pakistan have the chance to gain a foothold if they bat well. This could turn into a tight Test.

Cox is already showing himself to be difficult to leave out once Jacob Bethell returns from a knee injury, and one way England could retain him would be as wicketkeeper ahead of Smith.

On this occasion, they combined for the two telling batting contributions of the day, albeit in contrasting styles.

Abbas did the damage to the top order, with Root once again lbw with the keeper up to the stumps. When Lawrence was run out in a mix-up with Cox, England were 120-5 and teetering.

By this point, Cox had once again shown he has the technique and temperament for the highest level - he was patient as Pakistan dried up the scoring immediately after lunch.

Smith was given a life on 15 when keeper Muhammad Rizwan completely missed an edge off Ali. Reprieved, he dominated the strike and scoring in the stand with Cox, forcing the ball through the covers and whipping off his pads.

It took a moment of magic to part them. Salman, on as a sub, flew to his right at second slip to hold Cox, one-handed, off Khurram Shahzad.

Pakistan improve but could have been better

This was an opportunity for Pakistan to get back into the series. Had England won the toss it feels reasonable to suspect the home bowlers would have made life very difficult for the fragile visiting batting.

Abbas was magnificent. At one point he claimed three wickets for four runs in the space of 16 balls - Gay, Ben Duckett and Root.

He received support from Ali, whose three wickets were all batters bowled by the ball nipping down the Lord's slope. Brook, Smith and Ollie Robinson were his victims.

Two of Pakistan's drops did not prove too costly. Root was missed at third slip by Imam-ul-Haq on one, though the skipper was out for four. Shan Masood spilled a simple catch at mid-wicket when Lawrence had 10, then the same fielder made amends to run out Lawrence for 17.

Rizwan's miss was the most costly, symptomatic of the keeper and slip fielders appearing to stand too deep for most of the day with a number of edges not carrying through.

articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Joe Root's side reduced to 248-9 in rain-affected first day of second Test at Lord's
articles.summary: Pakistan reduced England to 248-9 on day one of the second Test at Lord's; Joe Root and England's top order struggled to score, while Jamie Smith and Jordan Cox made half-centuries; watch day two live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am on Friday
articles.body:
A deluge of rain postponed play until 12.20pm on Thursday afternoon, and much like the weather, England's day got off to a dreary start, with the hosts going 3-36 after just 10.3 overs, after Pakistan won the toss and elected to bowl.

After a week dominated by England's latest off-field incident involving bowler Brydon Carse , captain Joe Root's mood would not have lifted much as he was dismissed on Thursday by Abbas for just four runs.

That was further compounded by the cheap dismissals of Ben Duckett (17) and Emilio Gay (8), who were also snared by Abbas.

Abbas would take figures of 4-56 in, while Ali returned 3-67, producing three sensational 'nip-backers' to remove Harry Brook (15) as well as Jamie Smith (61) and Ollie Robinson (0).

With captain Babar Azam back in the side, Pakistan produced a much-improved performance from their innings and 103-run defeat at Headingley last week. But issues remain with Pakistan's fielding, with Mohammad Rizwan and his slips standing far too deep behind the wicket and saw multiple chances drop short in front of them.

England, meanwhile, rallied as the weather began to improve, with Jordan Cox (55) hitting back-to-back half-centuries, while Smith also brought up his fifty after what's been a lean period for the wicketkeeper-batsman.

"I was trying to ride the wave a little bit," Smith told Sky Sports .

"It is not the most free-scoring at times here - you can feel a bit out of rhythm but then catch up.

"I felt I scratched around at the start, but once I found the middle of the bat, it was slightly different to how I usually play, which is almost at top tempo to start with.

Gus Atkinson (34no) also performed well at the crease, and will return on Friday morning alongside Josh Tongue (1no), after play was suspended at 6.10pm on Thursday due to bad light, before the umpires chose not to return to the field.

Abbas gets Pakistan off to a flying start

After taking only one wicket against England at Headingley, Abbas was in prolific form on Thursday, first dismissing Gay with the help of the agile reflexes of Rizwan, who dived down the leg side to glove an edge from the Durham batter.

Pakistan had come close to dismissing Duckett early in the first over, with the England opener edging a ball out to the slips but the ball did not carry.

Duckett would face 20 deliveries before Abbas finally had him pinned lbw. The decision was initially given not out, looking like it was bouncing over the stumps, but Abbas was convinced it was plum, and he was proven right thanks to a successful review.

Root then arrived at the crease and initially rode his luck, with Imam-ul-Haq shelling an edge from the skipper at third slip, before Usman came close to taking a catch on the edge of the slip cordon.

In the next over, Abbas swung a ball into Root's leg stump, with the England captain unable to get his bat to the ball in time, as he was dismissed lbw.

Brook then entered the fray and angrily smashed Ali for four through square leg on his first delivery. But his stay at the crease was short-lived, with Brook skittled by a beauty from Ali, who jagged the ball back into his off stump, in what was perhaps the delivery of the day.

England found themselves 80-4 at lunch and in need of some stability, which came to a degree in the form of a partnership of 43 between Cox and Dan Lawrence, before the latter was run out following a bizarre mix up.

Cox hit seven boundaries on his way to his half-century, and after a couple of good starts with Brook and Lawrence, he and Smith set about mounting a score, with the pair posting a stand of 67 off 97 deliveries.

It was a moment of brilliance, though, from Salman Agha that broke the partnership, with the Pakistan all-rounder diving in the air to take a spectacular one-handed catch off an edge from Cox.

Smith would follow, with Ali taking both his and Ollie Robinson's wickets with two stunning nip-backers in the space of three deliveries.

Archer was the last of the England batters to be dismissed by Abbas, but not before he slogged a six back into the Lord's Pavilion, with Abbas later removing his bails before the players left the field.

articles.title: Brydon Carse: Durham happy to pick England bowler unless told otherwise
articles.summary: Durham coach Ryan Campbell says he is comfortable with selecting Brydon Carse, and will continue to do so unless they are told otherwise.
articles.body:
Durham coach Ryan Campbell says he is comfortable with continuing to select England bowler Brydon Carse, and says the club will continue to do so unless they are told otherwise.

Carse, 31, was briefly arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly after Durham's win over Derbyshire on Saturday, with images on social media showing Carse in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers.

He was removed from England's squad for the second Test against Pakistan after the Cricket Regulator began an investigation, but Durham picked him on Thursday for their County Championship match against Gloucestershire.

"He feels he's let the group down," Campbell told BBC Sport.

"The England team are trying to restart their whole way of going about it and he feels he's let them down.

"At the end of the day, he will have to live with that.

"I'm not going to stand here and say I've never made a mistake but what we can do is get our arms around him and make sure he doesn't make those mistakes again."

On Monday, Derbyshire Police said a man had been briefly detained outside Molly Malone's bar before being de-arrested.

They say they are looking into allegations of assault and their investigation remains ongoing.

Carse, who has 58 England caps, appears unlikely to be selected by the national team until the regulator completes its investigation. That process will be delayed by the police probe.

"[The regulator] is going to do their job, we're going to listen to what they say," Campbell said.

"When they give us a result, we'll act accordingly.

"Until then, everyone is free to play, he's free to play for Durham, and he'll continue to play."

The incident is the latest in a line of off-field issues involving players from England's men's team.

Carse's Durham team-mate Ben Stokes, the former England captain, was left out for a Test after breaking the team's midnight curfew earlier this year.

Asked if circumstances would require Durham to take a harder line with a player, Campbell said: "So far, I've never had to deal with that, so let's hope I don't have to deal with that."

Carse took a wicket in his first over against Gloucestershire and finished with figures of 2-51 from 12 overs as Division Two's bottom side were dismissed for 137.

articles.summary: Jamie Smith top-scores with 61 as England close day one of second Test versus Pakistan on 248-9; watch day two from Lord's, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am on Friday (play starts 11am)
articles.body:
Smith's spot in the side had been called into question at the start of the summer following a barren run of one half century in his prior 14 Test innings, where he was dismissed for single figures on seven occasions.

He scored 60 in his final innings of the series defeat to New Zealand, but was back under pressure after a poor dismissal to a top-edged pull in the first Test against Pakistan at Headingley.

"I have found it tough," Smith told Sky Sports Cricket as England closed day one at Lord's on 248-9 in their first innings . "It has been a lean period for me with some indifferent scores so I was trying to ride the wave a little bit.

"It is not the most free-scoring at times here [Lord's] - you can feel a bit out of rhythm but then catch up.

"I felt I scratched around at the start but once I found the middle of the bat, it was sightly different to how I usually play, which is almost at top tempo to start with. That seemed to help today."

Smith added: "Over the winter I had a bit of an issue with my front foot crossing over and it helped going back to Surrey at the start of the season and playing a block of red-ball cricket to rectify that.

"I felt I had good success doing that, batting up the order at number three, exposed to a newer, harder ball. I then altered that rhythm in the Test stuff batting at seven.

"I was trying to take a bit more time at Headingley last week, when on reflection I should probably have been a bit more aggressive from the start."

Smith's typical aggression with the bat was oft criticised during England's dismal 4-1 Ashes defeat over the winter in which he averaged just 23.44.

His first innings dismissal to part-timer Marnus Labuschagne in the final Test in Sydney was labelled 'witless' at the time , this a player who had taken to Test cricket like a dream in his first 12 Tests, averaging 58.64, until his form began to sour from midway through last summer.

"When he first came in, everything seemed to come to him easily, he played brilliantly," Sky Sports Cricket 's Nasser Hussain said.

"On the back of some low scores, and some poor shots, suddenly the spotlight has been on him... and it's how you react to that.

"I remember when he was playing really well, I admired the way he'd taken to Test cricket, his calmness - he seemed to have a low heart beat and things didn't seem to faze him.

"But then all of the things we were applauding him for, he then got hit by when it wasn't going so well. When he wasn't getting runs, his body language was being questioned - 'is he up for the battle?'

"For Jamie Smith, the fire is burning within. You don't have to always show it on the outside like I did or whatever."

articles.title: Daylen Lile homers as Nationals top Rockies 7-1 to split 4-game series
articles.summary: Daylen Lile homered and drove in two runs as part of a three-hit day, and the Washington Nationals beat the Colorado Rockies 7-1 to split their four-game ser...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Daylen Lile homered and drove in two runs as part of a three-hit day, and the Washington Nationals beat the Colorado Rockies 7-1 to split their four-game series Thursday.

Keibert Ruiz also went deep for Washington, which had dropped 12 of 15. The Nationals won a game started by a pitcher other than Cade Cavalli for the first time since Aug. 9.

Colorado fell to an NL-worst 52-82, clinching its eighth consecutive losing season. The Rockies were 1 for 9 with runners in scoring position and left 13 on base overall.

Lile led off the fifth inning with a drive to right off Gabriel Hughes (0-6) for his 18th home run this season . The left fielder was 8 for 15 with three homers and eight RBIs in the series.

Tom Cosgrove (1-2) pitched 1 2/3 scoreless innings in relief for his first win since his major league debut on April 29, 2023, a span of 89 appearances.

The Nationals scored twice in the first on Lile's bloop RBI single and Brady House 's sacrifice fly.

Colorado loaded the bases on a hit batsman and two walks in the third against Jake Irvin before Brett Sullivan 's infield single pushed across a run.

Washington made it 3-1 when Dylan Crews ' bases-loaded grounder in the fourth barely left the dirt area around the plate but still gave Jacob Young time to score from third.

Ruiz capped a three-run eighth with a two-run shot into the Nationals' bullpen in right off Jimmy Herget .

Hughes gave up four runs in five innings. He struck out three and yielded seven hits and four walks.

Irvin allowed a run on three hits and a career-high six walks in 4 1/3 innings while striking out six.

RHP Tomoyuki Sugano (12-7, 4.96 ERA) starts Friday as Colorado's road trip continues in Atlanta .

Rookie LHP Jackson Kent (0-2, 8.03) makes his fourth start Friday as Washington's homestand continues with the opener of a four-game series against Miami .

articles.title: 'Test cricket won': Shubman Gill after Sri Lanka force draw in Colombo
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India captain Shubman Gill said \"Test cricket won today\" after Sri Lanka fought hard to force a draw in the second Test in Colombo on Thurs.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India captain Shubman Gill said "Test cricket won today" after Sri Lanka fought hard to force a draw in the second Test in Colombo on Thursday. India had controlled much of the match and were in a strong position to push for victory.However, Sonal Dinusha produced another outstanding innings, scoring his second century of the match and staying unbeaten as Sri Lanka survived 154 overs.The result saw India finish the two-Test series with a 1-0 victory.'We did everything that we can'Gill said India made every possible effort during Sri Lanka's long second innings but could not break through their resistance."We fielded for about 150 overs, we did everything that we can. I don't think we could have done anything differently. Keeping the weather in mind, we could talk about these things (enforcing follow-on) only in hindsight."You take the best decision you can in the moment and something didn't go our way. But it was a brilliant game and I think Test cricket won today," Gill said after the match here on Thursday.Gill also gave credit to Sri Lanka for their fightback and said India could learn from the way the hosts responded under pressure."A lot of positives for us, learning from the opposition. The way they came back, it was tremendous to see. I don't think we could have done things differently. They bowled brilliantly in this game."Gill backs SutharGill also spoke highly of left-arm spinner Manav Suthar and backed him to play an important role for India in the future."How well he releases the ball, I think he's going to be crucial for us in the upcoming years," Gill said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Women's Asia Cup: Anything less than title will be a 'major disappointment' for Harmanpreet Kaur's India
articles.summary: Cricket News: India have won seven of the nine Women's Asia Cup editions played so far, across ODI and T20I formats, making them the most successful team in the his.
articles.body: India have won seven of the nine Women's Asia Cup editions played so far, across ODI and T20I formats, making them the most successful team in the history of the tournament.Given the historic dominance of the Indian team in the tournament, former India cricketer and ex-women's team coach WV Raman believes anything less than a title in the upcoming 2026 Women's Asia Cup would be a "major disappointment" for Harmanpreet Kaur's team."Pakistan and Sri Lanka will be tough competition for India, and let's not also discount Thailand, because they've shown a lot of enthusiasm, they've shown they've got some real good talent there, and you cannot take them lightly, too. As far as the Indian team is concerned, I think anything less than a victory will be seen as a major disappointment," Raman said in an exclusive interview with TimesofIndia.com, organised by Sony Sports Network.India lost the 2024 Women's Asia Cup final to Chamari Athapaththu's Sri Lanka by eight wickets in Dambulla, and Raman said "India can regain the Asia Cup" in Dubai.However, the road ahead is not as smooth for India as it seems. India have been missing two of their pace-bowling all-rounders, Amanjot Kaur and Kashvee Gautam, for over five months, and just before the Asia Cup they faced another setback as Jemimah Rodrigues was also ruled out of the tournament due to a hamstring injury.Pratika Rawal is in the side, but where should she bat?Pratika Rawal has received her maiden India T20I call-up as Jemimah was ruled out of the tournament, and is expected to walk straight into the playing XI when India face Thailand on Sunday. However, the bigger question is where the right-handed batter fits into India's batting order."Pratika Rawal has done extremely well in Test cricket. She's done well in ODIs, but in T20s, we haven't seen much of her so far. And also the other thing that they need to work out is her slot in the batting order. So where does she bat is something they've got to try and work out," former women's team coach Raman said.Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana will most likely not be separated as an opening pair, and Bharti Fulmali and Richa Ghosh could play the role of lower-order enforcers. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur bats at four when Jemimah plays at three in T20Is; however, Raman argued that Kaur should instead bat at three in the Asia Cup."I doubt if they will have Pratika Rawal at number three. I would rather imagine that Harmanpreet Kaur herself might bat at number three because she needs to spend a lot of time there at the crease, have more overs at her disposal to try and pace the innings," WV Raman said in an interview with TimesofIndia.com, adding, "Will India play Pratika at number four is something that will be a big question. As I see it, they need to obviously find ways and methods to use the 20 overs allotted to them in the most productive manner possible. So it's up to them to try and see."Longer rope for FulmaliFulmali ended her seven-year exile from international cricket earlier this year when she was picked for the South Africa tour and was also retained for the T20 World Cup.Among all the batters who have faced at least 100 balls in the Women's Premier League (WPL) since 2024, India's Richa Ghosh (155.05) and Bharti Fulmali (149.76) are at number two and three in terms of the strike rate, respectively.However, India dropped Fulmali from the team after just one innings in the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup where there campaign ended in the group stage.The former India cricketer said that the Women's Asia Cup is the ideal tournament to give Fulmali consistent chances."If they have plans for Fulmali in the near future or for the next couple of years, to be an integral part of the batting unit, then probably this is as good an opportunity as they'll get to try and give her a lot of chances and see how she fares," WV Raman said."Fulmali has the reputation of being a big hitter. She was picked up in the side about six years ago. Then again, she was out in the wilderness. Then again, she's come back, and then she's gone out, and she's come back. I think this is something that needs to be looked at very seriously because you're not doing anybody a favour by just giving them one odd chance here and there sporadically," he added.The former coach of the women's team also emphasized that India should look at the Asia Cup as a tournament where they begin preparation for the 2028 Women's T20 World Cup after their unceremonious group-stage exit in the 2026 T20 World Cup."They (India) can look at this Asia Cup as a platform from which they'll start planning for the next T20 World Cup in terms of planning, in terms of working out different combinations, looking at various options. So that will be a good thing to do starting from this Asia Cup, and even though you can't equate a terrific performance in the T20 World cup to a victory in Asia cup, if they go on to win this Asia cup, as we are expecting them to, it'll provide them some solace after probably the unexpected early exit in the T20 World Cup," WV Raman noted.Tune-In: Watch Women's Asia Cup 2026 live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD & Sony LIV.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: PCB threatens player protest after Atherton’s interview with Imran Khan’s sons at Lord’s
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has reportedly raised an objection with Sky Sports after former England captain Michael Atherton interviewed the two .
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has reportedly raised an objection with Sky Sports after former England captain Michael Atherton interviewed the two sons of Imran Khan during the lunch break on the opening day of the Test at Lord’s.According to Cricinfo, the PCB complained to the broadcaster over the decision to air the 18-minute interview with Suleiman Khan and Kasim Khan, which focused on their father’s health and concerns over his safety in prison.The episode created an unusual off-field controversy around the Test, with the PCB reportedly even considering whether Pakistan’s players should remain off the field when play was due to resume for the second session.PCB warned of possible player protestAtherton conducted the interview with Suleiman and Kasim on Wednesday at Lord’s, a day before the Test began. Sky Sports had also used a preview of the conversation in its coverage ahead of the match.According to Cricinfo, the PCB contacted Sky Sports before lunch on Thursday and objected to the planned broadcast. The board reportedly warned that Pakistan’s players could refuse to return to the field if the interview was aired.Sky Sports initially held back the segment before eventually showing it during the lunch interval.The interview was not broadcast in Pakistan because state broadcaster PTV holds the television rights for the series.Imran’s sons speak about his healthDuring their conversation with Atherton, Suleiman and Kasim discussed their concerns about their father's condition and safety while he remains in prison.The brothers also spoke about their efforts to ensure that Imran receives appropriate medical treatment.The former Pakistan captain and 1992 World Cup-winning skipper has been incarcerated for around three years, with his health and access to medical care becoming an increasingly prominent concern for his family.His sons have stepped up their public calls for greater access to medical treatment in recent weeks.Supreme Court order adds to concernsThe latest controversy comes after Pakistan's Supreme Court last week directed that Imran be admitted to Shifa Hospital in Islamabad.However, instead of being taken to the hospital named in the directive, Imran was taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) for a medical check-up before being returned to prison.His sisters and sons have alleged that the authorities did not follow the court's directive. They have also continued to demand that Imran be examined by his own doctor.The developments have prompted former international cricketers to publicly call for better medical care for the former Pakistan captain.Atherton among former captains backing ImranLast week, 21 former international captains, including Atherton, signed a letter to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urging authorities to ensure that Imran receives proper medical attention while in custody.The signatories included former captains from India, Australia, England, New Zealand and the West Indies.It followed another appeal in February, when 14 former international captains wrote to the Pakistan government on the issue. Reports said that letter did not receive a response.The PCB has not publicly commented on the reported complaint against Sky Sports.The Pakistan government has previously rejected allegations that Imran has been mistreated in prison or denied access to his family and legal representatives.Speaking to the Associated Press last week, the government said Imran had received more than 900 visits from relatives, lawyers and doctors since his imprisonment in August 2023.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘It would have been better if we got the win’: Devdutt Padikkal’s honest reaction after Player of the Series award
articles.summary: Cricket News: Devdutt Padikkal admitted the Player of the Series award came with mixed feelings after India settled for a draw in the second Test against Sri Lanka .
articles.body: Devdutt Padikkal admitted the Player of the Series award came with mixed feelings after India settled for a draw in the second Test against Sri Lanka at the SSC Ground on Thursday.Padikkal finished the two-Test series as India's leading batter, scoring 328 runs and registering two centuries. He stepped up impressively after B Sai Sudharsan was ruled out through injury, showing composure on slow and turning pitches across the series.India ultimately secured a 1-0 series victory after winning the opening Test, but Sri Lanka held firm in the second match. Sonal Dinusha's unbeaten 133 played a crucial role in helping the hosts survive the final day and force a draw.Speaking after receiving the Player of the Series award, Padikkal admitted the individual honour would have meant more had India completed a clean sweep."It's great, but it would have been better if we got the win in this game. I think the two pitches were quite similar. It was pretty slow here, but at the end of the day the batters got better at playing on such surfaces and that showed over the last couple of days," Padikkal said.Padikkal stresses importance of clear plansThe left-hander also explained the approach required from batters when playing on sluggish surfaces where scoring freely can be difficult.According to Padikkal, success on such pitches comes down to preparation, clarity and trusting the plans developed before going out to bat."It takes a lot of clarity. You need to have clear plans. Everyone came with their own plans, and the way the batsmen applied themselves showed out there."Padikkal's performances were particularly significant given his return to India's Test setup after spending time away from the side. Rather than focusing on the setbacks that came before his recall, he said the priority was to keep working and make the most of every opportunity."You want to play for the country, so you keep working hard and try to help your teammates out and take your opportunities when you get them. It's important that you forget that as fast as possible and move on to the next ball, and that's what I tried to do."Padikkal puts team ahead of batting positionDespite establishing himself as a dependable option in the top order, Padikkal insisted he has no preference when it comes to his exact position in the lineup.The 24-year-old said his priority is simply to score runs and contribute to team victories, regardless of where he is asked to bat."Honestly, I'm just happy to score runs. It doesn't matter what position. The team must win, and as long as I'm contributing to that, I am happy. We are a very young side. Important that we continue to learn. Everyone is really hungry and looking forward to doing that and getting better," he concluded.Padikkal's 328 runs and two centuries made him one of the standout performers of India's Sri Lanka tour, even though the second Test draw denied the visitors a series sweep.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shubman Gill reveals why Mohammed Siraj struggled for pace against Sri Lanka
articles.summary: Cricket News: India captain Shubman Gill has allayed concerns over Mohammed Siraj’s fitness after the pacer looked short of his usual pace during the drawn second T.
articles.body: India captain Shubman Gill has allayed concerns over Mohammed Siraj’s fitness after the pacer looked short of his usual pace during the drawn second Test against Sri Lanka, insisting the seamer is not injured and is simply regaining rhythm after a lengthy break from international cricket.Siraj was noticeably below peak pace at the SSC, often shortening his run-up and even bowling with the wicketkeeper standing up to the stumps. The fast bowler also suffered a heavy landing while attempting a catch in Sri Lanka’s first innings, fuelling speculation about a possible injury.“Siraj is not injured. He didn’t feel well even in the first match. He last played against Afghanistan in June, so he was coming back after almost a couple of months. It takes time for someone to come back into rhythm,” Gill said.The skipper acknowledged that Siraj’s pace had dipped through the series but backed the senior pacer to find his best form with more cricket under his belt.“Even in the first Test we felt that his pace was slow. But sometimes when you play more, you come back into rhythm. As far as injury is concerned, there is nothing,” Gill said.“It gets very frustrating,” Gill admitted about the draw and India’s failure to prise out the last few Lankan wickets. “We attacked a lot in the beginning, but as the match went on the wicket got slower. It wasn’t as if the ball wasn’t moving or spinning. It wasn’t a very flat wicket.”Although the draw dented India’s WTC final campaign, Gill remained optimistic.“I still think we’ve got a pretty good chance to qualify for the WTC final. If we play well in New Zealand and then win the Australia series at home, we’ll be in a good position to qualify,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sonal Dinusha leads Sri Lanka’s great escape as India’s spinners falter in Colombo
articles.summary: Cricket News: When was the last time a batter neutralised India’s spinners in a Test series with such authority?Cramping, exhausted but unrelenting, Sonal Dinusha a.
articles.body: When was the last time a batter neutralised India’s spinners in a Test series with such authority?Cramping, exhausted but unrelenting, Sonal Dinusha announced himself on the world stage in style, scoring an unbeaten 133 off 264 balls and combining with Sri Lanka’s dogged tail to script a sensational draw in the second Test at the SSC on Thursday.The 25-year-old left-hander, with his father applauding from the stands, registered his third century of the series and second in the match as Sri Lanka batted through the entire fifth day to deny India victory after being forced to follow on. It was a stirring display that once again highlighted the enduring romance and uncertainty of Test cricket.After scores of 100 and 84 in Galle and 101 and 133* in Colombo, Dinusha finished as the leading run-scorer of the series with 420 runs at 140.The draw allowed India to clinch the series 1-0, but it hurt their chances of reaching the 2027 World Test Championship (WTC) final. They now face the difficult task of winning five of their remaining seven Tests.“Test cricket won today,” India captain Shubman Gill remarked. That sounded like a platitude for Indian fans as they head into a challenging stretch of the WTC cycle with plenty to ponder. Sri Lanka’s escape evoked memories of Pakistan’s remarkable rear-guard in Mohali in 2005, when Kamran Akmal and Abdul Razzaq frustrated India on the final day to save a Test that appeared all but lost.India’s disappointment will centre largely around their spin attack. While left-arm spinner Manav Suthar impressed with 3/121 in 41 overs and ended the series with 16 wickets at 21.06, the others failed to deliver decisive blows on a fifth-day surface.Ravindra Jadeja claimed 3/94 but struggled to contain Dinusha, who repeatedly blunted India’s primary weapon. The veteran left-armer took eight wickets at 33.37 across the two Tests, modest returns by his lofty standards.Off-spinner Saransh Jain’s Test debut was equally underwhelming. After taking 2/69 in the first innings, he managed just 1/98 from 37 overs in the second. His selection ahead of the unavailable Kuldeep Yadav is certain to trigger scrutiny.When the players shook hands, Sri Lanka were 429/9 after batting 154 overs in their second innings. In an era when Tests often end inside four days, it was a classic exhibition of patience, technique and determination.Credit must also go to Sri Lanka’s curators, whose pitches ensured both Tests went the distance and produced compelling cricket. India appeared firmly on course for victory after securing a first-innings lead of 213 and enforcing the follow-on. Having won the first Test in Galle by 165 runs, they expected a repeat. Dinusha, however, had other ideas.The left-hander was the bedrock of Sri Lanka’s resistance, but the lower order played an equally vital role. Dinusha and Keshara Nuwantha (46 off 150 balls) added 112 for the seventh wicket, consuming 246 deliveries and 174 minutes. Even after Nuwantha fell to a sharply turning delivery from Suthar shortly after lunch, Sri Lanka’s resolve remained unbroken.Lahiru Kumara then contributed a priceless 12 from 90 balls in a ninth-wicket stand worth 47 runs from 170 deliveries. Last man Asith Fernando blocked 24 balls without scoring as India grew increasingly frustrated.Resuming on 229 for six, Sri Lanka steadily wore down the visitors. Despite obvious cramps, Dinusha remained focused on survival, reaching his century before guiding the tail through the closing stages.By tea, Sri Lanka were 383 for eight and firmly in control of the contest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
